newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest bourse index edges up in meagre turnover.
newsitem.headline: Budapest bourse index edges up in meagre turnover.

text.p: Share prices on the Budapest Stock Exchange traded mixed on Tuesday as many investors remained on the sidelines looking forward to new issues, resulting in the lowest daily spot share turnover this year.
"Investors are preparing for the upcoming share issues, they do not really want to jump into bourse-listed shares," said Attila Berecz of Raiffeisen Securities.
"There are some investors who are winding up their positions while new ones are rather uncertain," he said, adding that little impetus can be expected from foreign markets.
On Tuesday the BUX index closed at 5,530.56 points, up 18.45. Spot share turnover totalled 1.36 billion forints.
BUX futures closed mixed, up for three maturities and down for three other. March BUX edged lower 0.5 points to 5,577.00.
Certain stocks did move higher during the session but their rise was short-lived.
"Trade was encouraging at mid-session but prices of most stocks retreated to yesterday's levels by the end of the day," Berecz said, adding that the market seemed fragile.

Oil company MOL, chemicals maker TVK, OTP Bank, and hotelier Danubius posted some gains. MOL closed at 3,145 forints, down 10; TVK at 2,285, down 25; OTP at 3,850, up 15 and Danubius at 5,450, down 10.
Gas distributor company Primagaz, downgraded by Nomura Equity Research to 'hold' from 'buy' closed at 9,810 forints, down 190.
Planned share issues include MOL and pharmaceuticals Richter, pawnshop BAV Rt, commercial vehicle maker Raba Rt, curtain factory Gardenia Rt and agricultural machinery company Mezogep.
